claim_text: High supplemental vitamin C intake can increase urinary oxalate in some people and may be relevant to kidney-stone risk; stone history and total intake should be reviewed before high-dose supplementation.
health_goal_or_outcome: Support context-specific safety assessment and prevent unsupported supplement recommendations.

population.other_context: People with a history of kidney stones considering vitamin C supplements.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Dietary and/or supplemental products; verify exact formulation and label.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Vitamin C Health Professional Fact Sheet discusses oxalate and kidney-stone concerns associated with high supplemental intake.
limitations: Risk depends on dose, stone type and individual susceptibility; no individualized dose from this claim.
Exact source passages and underlying evidence require full appraisal before approval.
